title: Make the reply check cheaper

short.lead: The biggest repeated cost is a 5.5 second model call after nearly every reply; pick how to cut it so I can build it.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: After nearly every reply, a hook starts a second, smaller Claude model (Haiku) to check whether the reply claims something is impossible without proof. It runs only when the word list found no suspicious phrase, as a backstop for claims the list misses.
Nothing is built yet; this page only chooses how to cut the cost.

changes: Same check, runs only when it can matter
Measured with four runs, the median of three at 5,188 ms and one at 5,519 ms, against 63 ms with the call off (method and numbers: docs/qa/reply-check/timing.md). Every other hook costs about 70 ms.

Today: after a reply the word list (core.py _ROADBLOCK_RE and _STALL_RE) scans first; only when it finds nothing does _judge_check run a Haiku call that uses your usage allowance. The judge was added in #607 to catch what the list misses.

Option A runs the judge only when a wider word list matches. That narrows #607, and the 2026-11-24 Speed first decision rejected making the judge opt-in, so approving A would need a new decisions entry.
You would wait about 5 seconds less after replies the wider list skips. How many replies that is has not been counted: unverified.
choices: How should the reply check get cheaper?
Only run it when a wider word list flags the reply

Skips the 5 s call on replies the wider list passes. The wider list would add phrases such as 'could not' and 'unable to', which an earlier change removed to cut false alarms. A claim the list misses goes unchecked.
Run it in the background and show the verdict on the next turn
No waiting, but a background process must outlive the hook and a later hook must read its result. With no next turn, as in an unattended run, the warning is lost.
Skip it when the turn ran no tools and the reply has no negation
Cheap to test from the transcript the hook already reads; not yet tried, so its saving is unknown.
Keeps full coverage; the 5 s stays on nearly every reply.
A removes the wait on replies the wider list passes; it can still block a reply that list matches, but not a claim the list misses.
